scope: Additional JK/MotS model-surface techniques and corrections from retained original sources. Original synthesis; no raw source bodies or third-party assets included.
method: Offline read-only corpus search, selected complete forum/tutorial texts and Discord own-message bodies inspected, retained capture hashes checked. No fresh runtime test or external request.

queries.fts5: skin AND (palette OR colormap OR cmp)
(model OR skin OR 3do) AND (mipmap OR mipmaps)
(model OR skin OR 3do) AND (uv OR seam OR seams)
(model OR skin OR 3do) AND (transparent OR transparency)
("vertex color" OR "vertex colors" OR "vertex lighting") AND (blender OR model OR 3do)
(normals OR smoothing) AND (export OR exporter OR Blender)
(mipmaps OR colorkey OR "color key" OR RGB565) AND (mat OR model OR skin)
(seam OR seams OR bleed) AND (texture OR mat OR UV)

coverage.limit: Ranked searches are not an exhaustive review. Duplicate URLs, pages and messages can affect counts. One previously cited CosmoDNA source contributes newly synthesized technique detail; JKPaint continuation read.
excluded_scope: Jedi Outcast / Jedi Academy character and UV tutorials
world design, fog and level lighting recipes
uncorroborated converter diagnoses treated as successful fixes

sources.title: Mastering the MATs
sources.author: The Tynar
sources.claim: Separate value painting from color painting: preserve the source palette, edit a 24-bit grayscale version, paint color on a duplicate, Multiply the two, then quantize back to the intended palette.
sources.difference_from_1_2_and_limits: Adds an attributed artist recipe, including a face example, to the existing high-level hand-painting option. Authored historical tutorial; images not independently inspected here. The author acknowledges that the standalone example looked less good with the complete skin. Preserve model-space inspection and do not adopt the tutorial’s demo-save workaround or claim that more expensive paint software guarantees quality.

sources.title: Skins - The Massassi Temple
sources.author: CosmoDNA
sources.source_date: 1998-07-23 (catalog date from existing source ledger; tutorial body undated)
sources.claim: Keep the new face nose and brow aligned with the donor geometry; blend through palette color ramps. The tutorial then raises color depth, applies a small Gaussian blur, and reloads the target palette, warning that contrasting adjacent colors can quantize into muddy intermediate pixels.
sources.difference_from_1_2_and_limits: Previously cited for packaging and palettes, but its actual painting technique and failure mode were not synthesized in 1.2. The .50–.65 blur radius belongs to that historical image/editor example. Mirroring of its front-face texture is model-specific, not a general rule for all 3DOs. Palette-index transparency and renderer behavior require separate checks; do not universalize its black-pixel shorthand.

sources.title: Texture FAQ - The Massassi Temple
sources.author: Rosebud
sources.claim: For a repeating source, offset each layer by half its dimensions and repair the exposed seam with cloning or drawing. Keep highlights/shadows on separate layers. Prefer controlled brush edges over repeatedly blurring then sharpening.
sources.difference_from_1_2_and_limits: Adds a concrete seam-repair recipe and reversible painted-light organization. This is general texture authoring, transferable only to deliberately repeating model materials; it is not UV-island seam repair or a model bake. Painted directional light remains an optional style choice. The footer says 2001–2002 but does not establish a precise publication date. Photographic/donor overlays still require rights.

sources.title: JKPaint Beta Testing - Jedi Knight and Mysteries of the Sith Editing Forum - The Massassi Temple Forums Archive
sources.author: UGG
sources.post_or_section: posts #12, #14 and #16; full page and continuation read
sources.claim: JKPaint distinguishes adding an animation frame/cell from adding lower-resolution mip levels. With Generate mipmaps checked, adding a frame builds its mips; otherwise use Add mipmap. UGG explains the expected halving sequence, with 128×64 → 64×32 → 32×16 → 16×8 as an example.
sources.difference_from_1_2_and_limits: Adds an actual converter procedure and the author’s correction to ambiguous specs wording. Preserve the distinction between a base image, animation cells and mip levels. Beta crash reports in the same thread prevent treating this as universal converter reliability; do not promote its claimed 16-cell limit to an engine theorem. The continuation page adds no correction to the selected procedure.

sources.title: Problems with transparency - Jedi Knight and Mysteries of the Sith Editing Forum - The Massassi Temple Forums Archive
sources.author: money•bie; Emon; LKOH_SniperWolf; ProdigyOddigy
sources.claim: A transparent 3DO in front of another 3DO produced different results from combining the geometry. Emon reports that Blocks Light did not fix translucency; LKOH_SniperWolf cites JED’s CalcLighting functions as its editor-only use. ProdigyOddigy reports an asymmetric architecture-flag experiment and remaining stray triangles.
sources.difference_from_1_2_and_limits: Adds a counterexample to a common flag-fix recipe. The original example is scenery, so transfer only the diagnosis of layered 3DO transparency relevant to hair, visors, overlapping cloth or effects. Do not turn architecture flags into a player-model recommendation, a numeric layer limit, or the disputed 80% success claim. JED source was not independently checked in this pass.
